question: The Commission’s strategy for islands highlights the importance of territorial cohesion and reliable year‑round ferry connections between islands and the mainland. With that in mind: 1.

Can a Member State waive its overall responsibility for pursuing the objectives of economic, social and territorial cohesion set out in Articles 174 and 175 TFEU and the EU strategy for islands by making local authorities responsible for the provision of ferry services to islands to which there is no bridge, or do the national authorities remain responsible for ensuring that national arrangements and funding do not significantly impair the islands’ links to the mainland?

When a local authority significantly reduces an island’s only physical link to the mainland where there is no bridge to the island concerned, should the Member State ensure that an assessment is carried out of the implications for residents, businesses, public services and the viability of the island in the light of Articles 174 and 175 TFEU and the principle of the ‘island-proofing mechanism’ before the reduction is implemented?

Is it compatible with the EU strategy for islands for a national funding and responsibility model to allow for such a link to be significantly reduced for reasons relating to local authority finances, without an independent national assessment being made of the territorial consequences and the need for national support and compensation instruments?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.11.2026) The EU strategy for islands1 creates a common EU policy framework guiding EU action and supporting Member States in steering their programming and policies implementation by addressing the interconnected islands’ realities. In the strategy, the Commission invited Member States to take islands’ connectivity challenges into account in their national transport plans.

It further invited Member States to maintain and expand reliable year-round ferry services to secure consistent islands-mainland connections and to leverage public service obligations, compensatory mechanisms and targeted subsidies, where appropriate.

Although strengthening economic, social and territorial cohesion is one of the EU’s policies under the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU2, neither the Treaty nor the EU strategy for islands imposes specific requirements concerning ferry service levels, national funding or impact assessments.

The organisation and financing connections to islands, including the allocation of responsibilities between national and local authorities, remain Member States’ responsibility. Under Regulation (EEC) No 3577/923, Member States may impose public service obligations or conclude public service contracts to ensure adequate ferry connections where market conditions do not guarantee sufficient services.
It is for the Member States to determine which ferry connections require public service obligations to ensure an adequate level of service, considering local needs and circumstances.
1 Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament, the Council, the European Economic and

Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions EU strategy for islands, COM (2026) 520 final. 2 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=uriserv%3AOJ.C_.2016.202.01.0001.01.ENG&toc=OJ%3AC%3A2016%3A202%3ATO C#C_2016202EN.01004701. 3 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A01992R3577-20130701.
